people are willing to exert themselves on the behalf of the group, but that they are motivated by different concerns, depending on the way they are respected.

group members are motivated to increase their efforts for the group when they feel that they are respected and accepted by their group, or when they feel that their acceptance into the social group is in doubt.

group members are motivated to increase their discretionary efforts on behalf group goals when their group membership is threatened, either from the outside by the lack of intragroup respect or from the inside by the lack of acceptance into the group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
people can be motivated by both group-focused and self-focused concerns to engage in efforts on behalf of their group.
the same behavior (e.g., increased effort) can have different underlying motives (i.e., affective commitment vs. anxiety) depending on how group members are treated by their peers.
group members can be motivated to exert themselves on the behalf of their group by different types of concerns, depending on whether they are respected or disrespected.
